title: Boundary-kernel image on a first-quadrant total diagonal
statement: For an integer-indexed first-quadrant bicomplex M in a Grothendieck abelian category and integers 0<=q<=n, the image of the degree-n component of the totalized good horizontal truncation inclusion equals the second filtration step n-q [def-sp-double-complex-total] intersected with the inverse image under the total differential of the next-degree second filtration step n-q+1.

source.document: Stacks Project, Derived Categories and Homology

proof.text: In degree n the total is the finite direct sum of M^(p,n-p) for 0<=p<=n. Its second filtration step n-q is the sum over p<=q. The inverse-image condition is the kernel of its total differential followed by projection modulo the next vertical step. Every vertical differential and each horizontal differential from p<q already land in that next step. Only the outgoing horizontal differential of the boundary p=q survives, so the intersection is the direct sum of the full strict terms and its boundary kernel. The good horizontal truncation has precisely these terms. Use the direct-sum inclusions and kernel lifts to prove both subobject containments. At q=0 the strict direct sum is empty and the same kernel argument applies.

lean.statement:
theorem good_truncation_total_boundary_image
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} C]
    (M : HomologicalComplex₂ C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
    (hM : ∀ p r : ℤ, p < 0 ∨ r < 0 → IsZero ((M.X p).X r))
    (q : ℤ) (hq : 0 ≤ q) (n : ℤ) (hqn : q ≤ n) :
    imageSubobject ((total.map (CochainComplex.ιTruncLE M q)
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).f n) =
      (M.secondFiltration n).step (n - q) ⊓
        (Subobject.pullback ((M.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).d n (n + 1))).obj
          ((M.secondFiltration (n + 1)).step (n - q + 1))
